segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: When I put the twenty-one and twenty-three side by side, it wasn't a close call — two more sessions, dashboard hookup, follow-ups included, for two grand more. The middle package just looked thin next to it. ... that smaller option had sort of fallen out of view — the contrast between the other two was what I was reacting to, even though I had the runway to sit down and actually map Vendor A against the scope properly.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant lets the near-priced inferior full-service option frame Vendor C and does not independently assess whether Vendor A meets the three-flow scope, despite ample time.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I went with the first candidate. His shipped work at that company was the caliber we wanted, and I figured someone operating at that level would naturally bring solid documentation and communication habits too. ... I extended trust from the visual work to the rest of it.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant generalizes prestige and visual polish to unverified documentation and communication abilities, despite the other candidate's directly relevant process evidence and available trial task.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: That my adjustments were doing something. I asked the Analytics Lead for more manual control so I could keep pushing on it. ... we had time to just wait for a bigger sample or run an isolated test. But the timing lined up so well with what I'd changed that it felt like real evidence.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant attributes an underpowered, confounded uptick to their own manual rule changes and acts on that attribution despite the Analytics Lead's warning and schedule slack.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: The bump partly reversed once the email campaign ended, and she noted the actual driver was still unconfirmed.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This later uncertainty update acknowledges reversal and unresolved causality; it contains no hidden manifested bias instance.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Participant: I argued to keep customizing the legacy piece. We'd already sunk three sprints in, and switching felt like giving that up, even with time to spare. ... Probably better, if I'm honest. But it was hard to treat the three sprints as separate from the decision in front of me.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Past effort is used to justify continuation even though the forward-looking one-sprint migration estimate is better and remaining runway is sufficient.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: An intermediate option (Vendor B) is priced close to the target option (Vendor C) but offers strictly less value, making Vendor C appear to be the obviously superior deal relative to Vendor B, which pulls attention away from independently assessing whether the cheaper Vendor A package actually matched the research scope.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Attraction effect is an established scholarly alternate name for the decoy effect; the finding describes the inferior near-priced option making Vendor C attractive and pulling attention from Vendor A.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: Full match: the finding captures the three-option B/C contrast, diversion from independently assessing the cheaper sufficient A option, and the comparative vendor-evaluation operation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes are verbatim and attributed to the Participant; the central comparison and counterfactual are directly present.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision point 3: personalization rules-engine activation interpretation
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Overattribution of an observed metric change to the designer's own specific manual action, despite acknowledged insufficient statistical power and unresolved confounding factors, even though waiting for more data was schedule-feasible.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Confirmation bias is a near-neighbor construct: it concerns favoring evidence that confirms a belief, whereas the hidden label names overestimating personal causal control. The RAG does not use the hidden label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: Full operational overlap: the finding identifies the self-attributed causal interpretation of the uptick, the below-threshold sample and concurrent email confounds, and the decision to seek expanded authority despite those warnings. Its framing emphasizes confirmatory evidence weighting, so the label remains a near neighbor.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quoted dashboard, warning, and counterfactual statements are verbatim and attributed to the Participant; the supplied corpus citation is separate from interview-evidence validity.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Continuation of the design approach is justified primarily by the magnitude of prior invested effort rather than a forward-looking comparison of remaining costs and benefits, even though remaining schedule slack could absorb the migration cost.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Sunk cost fallacy is an established scholarly alternate for Sunk Cost Bias.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: Full match: three prior sprints dominate the continuation decision despite a better forward-looking migration estimate and known defects.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes are verbatim, speaker-correct, and include the direct rationale and counterfactual isolation of prior effort.
